on Wednesday announced that the European Commission approved its inhaler therapy Trixeo Aerosphere as a late-line maintenance option for patients aged 12 years and older with asthma, expanding the drug's availability in the EU.

The decision specifically allows its use as a maintenance treatment for asthma in the above group of patients whose symptoms remain insufficiently controlled despite prior therapy with a combination of a medium-dose inhaled corticosteroid and long-acting beta2-agonist.
Marketed as Breztri Aerosphere in the U.S., the triple-combination therapy is already available in the region for adults with chronic obstructive pulmonary disease.

Its latest approval follows a positive opinion from an expert panel of the EU drug regulator in July that recommended a label expansion for Trixeo Aerosphere for asthma, a condition affecting nearly 43M people in Europe.

title: AstraZeneca granted EU label expansion for COPD therapy, Trixeo in asthma
